It should always be presented nicely. Any tips for the egg fried rice, how do you cook the pork?

for pork fried rice, use a good piece of gammon. a big gammon joint if you're oven roasting it, but its just as good to use a gammon steak, chop it and throw it into the wok with a little oil. add some chopped onions and peppers, some diced chilli, black pepper maybe a few other bits of veg, and fry it up. (for oven roasting, little to no seasoning is needed, just roast it up, cut off enough to feed everyone, and add the meat after the veg is cooked, just before the rice, since it'll already be nice)

the rice needs to be pre-cooked, then allowed to cool and dry out a little. i do this part first, then let it sit in a fine sieve while i heat the wok and fry up the meat and veg. when you add it to the pan, it'll need to have the right consistency, because you'll be mixing it around to get it all fried, and if its too wet, it'll turn to a paste while you work it.

so add the rice once the meat and veg look ok, and give it a generous glug of soy sauce, or Worcestershire sauce, or both. (i dont add salt when doing the meat, because soy sauce is salt heavy, and should be the only salty thing you need to add.) mix it gently until the rice is nicely coated with sauce, then crack an egg or two into a cup, give it a quick whisk together and pour into the wok. quickly and gently mix again, so everything gets a nice coating of fried eggy-ness. when the egg is cooked, which wont take long, serve it.

it might take a time or two to perfect, but its a good simple recipe for a crowd pleasing dish :)

Here is a recipe for my own BBQ sauz.

Kobolds BBQ sauz

1 big bottle of HFCS free ketchup

1 big bottle of Worcestershire

1/2 an onion minced

8 thick strips of bacon minced

1 whole bulb of garlic minced

3 tablespoons of molasses

3 tablespoons of chili powder

3 table spoons of paprika

1 tablespoon of cumin

cayenne pepper to preference of heat 1 teaspoon at least

salt and pepper to taste

Mix all wet ingredients together then add seasoning. Bring to a quick boil then turn to low and simmer till it is the thickness you desire. Meanwhile pan fry the bacon, when it is almost crisp add the onions, till they turn just barely caramelized, add the garlic and continue till the garlic is caramelized. Add this mixture to the simmering sauce mix and continue simmering till it is the thickness desired. Leave it chunky or puree till smooth as preferred. Chill the sauce and enjoy on your favorite foods.

If it doesn't fit back into the ketchup bottle then its not simmered down enough.

I am an amazing cook, not gonna lie. Experimenting in the kitchen is a hobby/past-time of mine, so it's inevitable that I'd improve substantially over the past half of my life. After lots of trial and error, finally got the feel for making some amazing homemade pizza. Made my first pan pizza yesterday, and if I threw it in a cardboard box you wouldn't be able to tell the difference from a decent pizza joint.

Since it's the thing at the top of my mind, atm, as it was my latest project: I'll share a few tips for that. To make two, medium-large pizzas in less than three hours (normally you'd have to prep the day before):

  • 3 cups of all purpose flour
  • a cup of (very) warm water (but not so hot that you can't comfortably stick your hand in it)
  • one tablespoon of sugar
  • one teaspoon of salt
  • 3 tablespoons of olive oil
  • 3 slightly heaping teaspoons of normal yeast

Mix everything mentioned above in a bowl, with an electric hand mixer for ~3 minutes, minus two cups of flour, on medium speed. Once you're done, add in one more cup of flour, and stir it around until it thickens up to the point that it doesn't stick to the bowl anymore. dust your kitchen counter with some of the remaining flour, and plop that bad boy on there. Knead it for ten minutes.

Basically, roll it out with your palms, fold it in half, rotate 90º and do that over and over again for ten minutes. Keep adding a bit of flour as the ball absorbs it, until you've added all of it, and the dough is springy enough that when you poke it with your finger, it bounces right back. Might take less than or more than ten minutes, depending on how on point your kneading game is.

Coat the ball with a bit of olive oil (so it doesn't dry out while rising), and put it back in the bowl you used for mixing. Toss a sheet of plastic wrap on it, as well, but not tightly. Just nonchalantly throw it on there like you were making your bed in a hurry (the dough needs space to puff up). Leave it somewhere warm for forty minutes. When you're done, plop it back on the counter (careful, it's a lot softer now than when you were giving it a shiatsu). Slice it in half.

Roll each ball out in to a circle, on top of a sprinkling of more flour or, preferably, corn meal. Best way I've found to do this is to alternate up/down and side/side, in perpendicular positions. Get it to, I dunno, half a cm thickness (less if you like thin crust, more if you like it extra poofy). Put that on a tray (I bought a pizza pan). If you wanna make it a pan pizza (you fat fuck), toss enough olive oil in a pan that it coats the bottom of it up to 2mm in thickness. Brush with a bit more olive oil and do the plastic wrap thing again. Let it rise for another forty minutes.

But this time (and this is my little trial-and-error discovery), let it rise on top of your oven, while you have it preheating to 450ºF. Just set it on the burners, the extra warmth will have those bad boys puff up like a couple of bro-dudes when they see a group of good looking girls walk by.

Once the time is up, your oven should already be preheated. Add your sauce, cheese and toppings. Toss those filthy delinquents in to the oven like it's 1945, on the lower-middle rack, for ~17 minutes.

Grats, you just made a bomb-ass pizza. Two, actually.

One of my favorite dinners:

Kielbasa Stew

  • 1 whole kielbasa (the big ass sausages that your drunk uncle called a horse cock)
  • 1 head of cabbage
  • 8-10 carrots
  • 5-8 potatoes
  • Beef broth or bouillon
  • Cornstarch or instant mashed potatoes

Chop the kielbasa into slices about 1cm long and dump them into the broth. Let that simmer just below boiling for a while to let the sausage fat melt out. Cut up your cabbage, carrots and potatoes while you wait. Big chunks are encouraged because we're not fucking pussies.

Throw the cabbage, carrots and potatoes all in at once. The cabbage should be nice and overcooked by the time the carrots and potatoes are done. Stir it up and add cornstarch or instant potatoes until you get a nice stew-like consistency.
